text:
Darcy Kuemper played his 500th NHL game last week and it ended in a bad loss to the Islanders. A few days later he gave the Kings exactly what a team on a four-game winless run needs: 29 saves, no goals, and a 3-0 win in Boston that the rest of the roster did not entirely deserve.

By our replays of every shot, the Bruins win this game 57% of the time. Expected goals (the quality of the chances) finished 2.20 to 2.10 for Boston, and the Bruins outshot Los Angeles 29 to 22. Ty Anderson of 98.5 The Sports Hub watched the Kings and wrote that they were "dying to give one away," so careless with the puck, but that the Bruins never made them pay. Kuemper is the reason. He saved 2.2 goals more than his shots deserved, including a 21% look from Fraser Minten in the second, and finished with more wins added than anyone in the game.

The Kings' scoring came in small doses. Mats Zuccarello opened it at 15:46 of the first with a wrister off Erik Gustafsson and Brandt Clarke, a goal worth 8% going in. Andre Lee deflected in Scott Laughton's shot late in the second, which moved the Kings' win chance from 71% to 87%. Gustafsson, back after a three-game absence, sealed it at 16:53 of the third with Kuemper picking up the assist. Quinton Byfield led Los Angeles with four shots and 0.70 expected goals without scoring.

Boston coach Marco Sturm shuffled his top three lines to start the third, per Anderson, with Morgan Geekie moving up beside Elias Lindholm and David Pastrnak. The Bruins out-chanced the Kings 0.88 to 0.23 in that period and still got nothing past Kuemper. Michael DiPietro was fine at the other end, about what his 21 shots deserved, and was the third star. It was the kind of loss that stings more than a blowout: the Bruins did enough to win and the scoreboard never noticed.

For the Kings, a win like this buys a little breathing room. Kevin Fiala is back after nine months away following his Olympic injury, and if the goaltending holds like this, the rest of the lineup has time to find itself.
headline: Kuemper steals one in Boston
